blocks.text: 15. The Devil
The Chains of Materialism
Numbered fifteen, The Devil stands on a stone altar to which two figures, a man and a woman, are chained.
Unlike the liberating energy of the Fool or the spiritual ascent of the Hermit, this card represents the heavy descent into matter.
The Devil is the archetype of Materialism—the belief that only the physical world is real and valuable.
He represents the entrapment of the spirit by the flesh, symbolizing our addictions, obsessions, and the unchecked pursuit of pleasure that ultimately leads to slavery.
The Shadow Self
The Devil takes the form of Baphomet, a goat-headed deity representing the primal, animalistic side of human nature.
He is the "Shadow Self" described by Jung—the parts of ourselves we refuse to acknowledge and therefore project onto others.
He is not an external monster, but an internal one.
He is the sum of our fears, our shame, and our suppressed desires.
By facing him, we are actually facing the darkest corners of our own psyche.
The Illusion of Bondage
Look closely at the chains around the necks of the man and woman. They are loose.
The figures could easily slip them off and walk away, yet they remain.
This is the central lesson of the card: the illusion of bondage.
We are rarely held captive by external forces; rather, we are imprisoned by our own choices, our comfort zones, and our refusal to take responsibility.
The Devil does not hold us against our will; he simply offers us a comfortable cage, and we choose to stay.
The Agency of Obsession
The agency of this card is obsession.
While passion (The Lovers) expands us, obsession constricts us.
It is the narrow focus on a single desire—be it money, power, sex, or a person—to the exclusion of all else.
The Devil creates a feedback loop where the more we feed the hunger, the hungrier we become.
He represents the loss of perspective, where a part of life is mistaken for the whole of life.
An Invitation to Break Free
Drawing The Devil is a call to liberation.
It is a harsh wake-up call asking you to examine where you have given away your power.
It invites you to acknowledge your shadow, to stop blaming circumstances, and to realize that the door to your prison is unlocked.
It reminds you that the first step to freedom is admitting that you are bound.
